title: New Israeli Attacks Kill Eight Palestinians in Gaza in 24 Hours
text:
Eight Palestinians were killed and 31 wounded by Israel’s strikes, tank fire and drone attacks across the Gaza Strip in the past 24 hours, raising the enclave’s death toll to 73,470 since October 2023. An Israeli airstrike struck the Al-Hawja area inside the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, one of the enclave’s most crowded districts.
In the south, drone attacks wounded several people in a tent sheltering displaced families in Al-Mawasi, a coastal stretch of Khan Younis, according to field reports .
RELATED: Trump’s Gaza Peace Board Accused of Clearing War Evidence
The same southern area came under intense tank fire directed at temporary homes near the local cemetery. Hospitals admitted eight newly wounded people amid what the ministry described as continuing Israeli violations.
Rescue efforts remain paralyzed. Ambulance and civil defense crews have not been able to reach victims still trapped beneath the rubble and lying in the streets. Off the coast of Gaza City, the Israeli navy also detained a fisherman, health authorities said.
💢 “Why should a child filling up water die?”: Israeli attack kills four, including two children and a woman, in Gaza City
Eight others were also wounded in Tuesday’s attack in the Al-Katiba area of western Gaza City, where families had gathered to collect water.
“We were just… pic.twitter.com/IeJVDCT0wx
— Drop Site (@DropSiteNews) September 1, 2026 Toll Tops 73,000 The official balance puts the number of Palestinians killed since the offensive began on Oct. 7, 2023 at 73,470, with more than 174,000 wounded . Since the ceasefire took effect, the Israeli military has killed another 1,334 Palestinians, wounded 4,429 and allowed the recovery of 815 bodies, according to the Ministry of Health.
The attacks unfold amid constant breaches of the truce. Israeli forces continue shelling residential zones with artillery and launching airstrikes with warplanes and drones, destroying neighborhoods and infrastructure and killing civilians.
The scenes in Jabalia and Khan Younis show how little protection the ceasefire has offered families sheltering in camps and tents. People uprooted by months of bombardment were struck again inside the temporary homes meant to keep them safe.
Health workers warn that the death toll could climb as rescue crews gain access to collapsed buildings. The ministry has repeatedly reported that victims remain under debris because Israeli fire and access restrictions keep emergency teams away.

Palestinian health figures have been cited by international agencies as broadly reliable, though the real number of dead may be higher while access to some areas stays blocked.
